newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala harasses raped U.S. nun, laywer says.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala harasses raped U.S. nun, laywer says.

text.p: The Guatemalan courts are harassing U.S. nun Diana Ortiz instead of investigating her 1989 kidnapping, rape and torture, her attorney said on Wednesday.

"They're trying to intimidate her, and they're trying to deflect criticism by making it look like they are taking additional steps to investigate the case," lawyer Michele Arington told Reuters in a telephone interview from Washington.

Last September the Interamerican Human Rights Commission of the Organisation of American States concluded that Guatemalan government agents were responsible for the crimes against Ortiz and exhorted the Guatemalan government to investigate.
But the Guatemalan prosecutor who last week won the right to question Ortiz in writing said the nun failed to cooperate with Guatemalan and U.S. authorities.
"She's playing politics," said Braulio Guzman. He added, "they both are, she and the Guatemalan government."

Ortiz, a memmber of the Kentucky-based Ursuline order, disappeared on Nov. 2, 1989. She later testified she was forcibly taken by two Guatemalan men on a bus and then in a police car driven by a third Guatemalan in police uniform.
Ortiz, 38, who now lives in Washington, testified she was repeatedly raped, burned with cigarettes and interrogated for several hours.
A fourth man, whom she believed to be an American called "Alejandro," took her in a car, from which she escaped outside of Guatemala City the day after her abduction, she testified.
